items.title: Borel sigma-algebra of a product of second-countable spaces
items.statement: For second-countable topological spaces X,Y with the product topology, B(X×Y)=B(X)⊗B(Y).
items.strategy: Use the countable product basis to show every product-open set is a countable union of measurable rectangles, then use continuous coordinate projections for the reverse inclusion.
items.axiom_use: The proof uses only countable bases and finite products of countable sets; no choice principle is used.

items.title: Finite-window spatial observations and configurations
items.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a bounded Borel set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$. Under
Countable Choice every Borel subset of $\mathbb R^d$ is Lebesgue measurable
([[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]), so Lebesgue measure $\ell_d$ is
defined on each such set. Write $|A|:=\ell_d(A)$ for Borel $A$, and
$\mathcal B_W:=\{W\cap A:A\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^d)\}$ for the trace Borel
sigma-algebra on $W$. Every member of $\mathcal B_W$ is Borel in $\mathbb R^d$
because $W$ is Borel. Define $\ell_W:\mathcal B_W\to[0,+\infty]$ by
$\ell_W(A):=\ell_d(A)$. If $(A_k)$ is pairwise disjoint in $\mathcal B_W$,
then each $A_k$ and their union are Borel in $\mathbb R^d$, so countable
additivity of $\ell_d$ gives
$$\ell_W\!\left(\bigcup_k A_k\right)=\ell_d\!\left(\bigcup_k A_k\right)
=\sum_k\ell_d(A_k)=\sum_k\ell_W(A_k),$$
and $\ell_W(\varnothing)=0$. Thus $\ell_W$ is a measure on the trace sigma-
algebra. Since $W$ is bounded, $\ell_W(W)<\infty$
([[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]).
The only choice axiom used to regard $\ell_d$ as a measure in this library is
Countable Choice, as recorded in
[[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]].

The **finite configuration space on $W$**, denoted $\mathcal C(W)$, is the
measurable subspace of locally finite counting measures on $\mathbb R^d$
consisting of those $\eta$ with $\eta(W^c)=0$ and $\eta(\mathbb R^d)<\infty$.
It is measurable in the ambient evaluation sigma-algebra because both
$\eta\mapsto\eta(W^c)$ and $\eta\mapsto\eta(\mathbb R^d)$ are evaluation
maps for Borel sets.
Thus each $\eta\in\mathcal C(W)$ has a representation
$\eta=\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{x_i}$ for a finite $n\ge0$ and $x_i\in W$; repeated
locations are allowed and represent multiplicity. Its sigma-algebra is the
trace of the evaluation sigma-algebra: it is generated by
$\eta\mapsto\eta(B)$ for Borel $B\subseteq W$.

For a finite ambient configuration $\widetilde\eta$, its observation in $W$
is $\eta=\widetilde\eta|_W$, where
$\eta(B)=\widetilde\eta(B\cap W)$. The observation includes precisely the
locations belonging to $W$: a boundary location is included when and only
when it belongs to $W$. This convention does not replace $W$ by its interior
or its closure.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the library's construction of Lebesgue measure; no full Axiom of Choice or dependent choice is used.

items.title: Products of a measurable intensity over finite configurations are measurable
items.statement: For finite-valued Borel f on W, the occurrence product η↦∏_{x∈η}f(x), including multiplicity and empty product 1, is measurable on the finite-window configuration space.
items.strategy: Prove the assertion for simple functions from evaluation maps, then pass to an increasing simple approximation and its pointwise product limit.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the finite-window Lebesgue measure; the product-measurability argument itself uses no choice.

items.title: Finite-window pair counts are measurable
items.statement: For R≥0, S_R(η)=((η⊗η)(D_R)-η(W))/2 is measurable and counts unordered pairs of distinct atom occurrences at Euclidean distance at most R.
items.strategy: Show η↦(η⊗η)(A) is measurable on rectangles, extend to the product Borel sigma-algebra by Dynkin's theorem, then apply it to the closed distance set.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the finite-window Lebesgue measure; the pair-count measurability proof itself uses no choice.

items.title: Finite products of measures with densities have the product density
items.statement:
Let $\mu$ be any finite measure on $(W,\mathcal B_W)$, where $W$ and its
trace Borel sigma-algebra $\mathcal B_W$ are as in
[[def-finite-window-spatial-observation]]. Let $f:W\to[0,\infty]$ be
measurable with $\int_W f\,d\mu<\infty$, and put $\nu=f\,d\mu$.
For every integer $n\ge1$, the product measure $\nu^{\otimes n}$ on
$\mathcal B_W^{\otimes n}$ has density
$$F_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\prod_{i=1}^n f(x_i),$$
where products use the extended-product convention
$0\cdot(+\infty)=0$. For $n=0$, both product measures are the
unit mass on the one-point empty tuple and the product density is $1$.
items.strategy: Both measures are finite and agree on measurable rectangles by the product formula and Tonelli; uniqueness extends equality to the product sigma-algebra.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the finite-window Lebesgue measure; the finite product-density proof itself uses no choice.

items.title: Papangelou conditional intensity on a finite window
items.statement:
Let $W$, $\ell_W$, and $\mathcal C(W)$ be as in
[[def-finite-window-spatial-observation]]. Let $P_{\theta,b}$ be a specified
probability law on $\mathcal C(W)$; $b$ denotes a fixed exterior configuration
when the model uses a boundary condition, and is omitted when it does not. For
this fixed boundary convention, a jointly measurable function
$\lambda_\theta:W\times\mathcal C(W)\to[0,+\infty]$ is a
**Papangelou conditional intensity relative to $\ell_W$** for this law and
boundary convention; the notation $\lambda_\theta(u;\eta,b)$ displays the
fixed boundary label but $b$ is not an additional variable in its measurable
domain. Omit $b$ when there is no exterior condition or when the fixed
convention is clear from context. The defining identity holds when, for every
nonnegative product-measurable
$h:W\times\mathcal C(W)\to[0,\infty]$,
$$\mathbb E_{\theta,b}\left[\sum_{x\in\eta}h(x,\eta-\delta_x)\right]=\mathbb E_{\theta,b}\left[\int_W h(u,\eta)\lambda_\theta(u;\eta,b)\,\ell_W(du)\right].$$
The sum runs over atom occurrences, so $\eta-\delta_x$ deletes one
occurrence; if $b$ is used, it is fixed on both sides. The identity is the
definition of the Papangelou intensity used on this page. It does not assert
that every finite-window law has such a function.

The deletion operation and the resulting measurable random sum use
[[lem-deletion-of-one-point-is-measurable]]. On the occurrence domain, the
deletion-composition is measurable; extend it by zero off that measurable
domain and integrate against the evaluation kernel $K(\eta,B)=\eta(B)$. This
integral is the displayed sum, and its measurability follows from the
deletion map and [[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]], as
used in the deletion lemma.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the window's Lebesgue measure; the defining identity uses no further choice.

items.title: Finite-window point-process pseudolikelihood
items.statement: For fixed data η and fixed boundary b, define PL(θ;η)=∏_{x∈η}λ_θ(x;η-δ_x,b) exp{-∫_W λ_θ(u;η,b)du}, when the displayed factors and integral are finite; it is a criterion, not generally a joint likelihood.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the window's Lebesgue measure; the definition uses no further choice.

items.title: Finite-window Gibbs density relative to a Poisson reference
items.statement: Given a specified finite-window Poisson law Q, measurable support S_θ, and measurable energy H_θ, define a Gibbs law only when Z_θ=∫e^{-H_θ}1_{S_θ}dQ is finite and positive, with density Z_θ^{-1}e^{-H_θ}1_{S_θ}.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the window's Lebesgue measure; the density definition uses no further choice.

items.title: A finite Poisson process with atomless intensity is simple
items.statement: A finite Poisson point process with atomless finite intensity is almost surely simple.
items.strategy: Under the finite mixed-binomial representation, each pair of iid locations collides on a product-null diagonal; a finite union for each count and the countable Poisson mixture preserve nullity.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used by the finite-mixture and diagonal-null proof.

items.title: Finite-window spatial Poisson likelihood relative to unit rate
items.statement: For bounded Borel W and finite-valued Borel λ_θ≥0 with Λ_θ=∫_Wλ_θdx<∞, dP_θ/dP_0(η)=exp{|W|-Λ_θ}∏_{x∈η}λ_θ(x), where P_0 is unit-rate Poisson law and products count occurrences. The log likelihood up to |W| is Σ_{x∈η}log λ_θ(x)-Λ_θ, with value -∞ when an observed event has zero intensity.
items.strategy: Expand P_θ and P_0 with the finite mixed-binomial representation, rewrite each finite product measure by its product density, and verify ∫_A g_θ dP_0=P_θ(A) for every measurable A.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through Lebesgue measure. The formula explicitly supplies every parameter's density version, so no full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: Homogeneous Poisson rate MLE in a positive-volume window
items.statement: If |W|>0 and N(W)>0, the homogeneous rate MLE over ρ≥0 is N(W)/|W|. If N(W)=0, the supremum is at ρ=0, attained when zero is admitted and otherwise approached only as ρ↓0.
items.strategy: Subtract log likelihoods at ρ and N(W)/|W|, then use the mean value theorem to show log t-t+1≤0 with equality only at t=1; handle zero count directly.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the window's Lebesgue measure; no further choice is used.

items.title: A positive finite-window Gibbs density has its density-ratio Papangelou intensity
items.statement: If P has a finite, strictly positive density g relative to the unit-rate finite-window Poisson law, then λ_g(u;η)=g(η+δ_u)/g(η) satisfies the deletion-form Papangelou identity.
items.strategy: Apply the finite-intensity Mecke identity to the test function g(η)h(u,η-δ_u), using measurable single-occurrence deletion, then factor g(η+δ_u)=g(η)λ_g(u;η).
items.axiom_use: The finite-window measure uses Countable Choice through Lebesgue measure; the density-ratio argument itself uses no choice.

items.title: Homogeneous Poisson rate estimation at positive-count and zero-count boundaries
items.statement: For W=[0,2]^2, |W|=4, a three-point homogeneous Poisson pattern has MLE 3/4; an empty pattern has the rate-zero boundary supremum, attained only if zero belongs to the parameter space.

items.title: Exact and pseudo likelihoods for finite-window Poisson and Strauss models
items.statement: For a finite Poisson reference on W=[0,2]^2, the homogeneous Poisson pseudolikelihood is proportional to the exact likelihood. For the soft Strauss density with R=1/2, β>0, and 0<γ<1, compare the empty and one-point patterns to show the pseudolikelihood is not proportional to the exact joint density.
items.strategy: Bound the Strauss normalizer above by E_{P0}[β^N] and below by the empty-pattern probability, derive its Papangelou ratio from Mecke, then compare exact and pseudo likelihood ratios for empty and one-point observations.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the window's Lebesgue measure; no full Axiom of Choice is used.
